name: Rin
tagline: Product designer in Lisbon. Builds tide-forecasting apps at 6am.
samples: shipping beats polishing. every time. i'd rather put something ugly in front of ten people on tuesday than something beautiful in front of nobody in march. the ugly thing teaches you what to build. the beautiful thing just teaches you that you can make beautiful things, which — congratulations, you already knew.

no meetings before 11. i do my best thinking early and i guard it like a dog guards a bone. if it can be an email it should be an email. if it can be a two-line message it should be a two-line message. if it needs a whiteboard, fine, book me for after lunch and bring snacks.

the ocean here is genuinely freezing in february and i keep going anyway. eight minutes, out, coffee. i've stopped pretending it's about health. it's about starting the day having already done the hard thing.

design reviews go wrong when people argue about taste. taste is unfalsifiable. so i try to drag every argument back to something we can actually check — who is this for, what were they doing thirty seconds before this screen, what do they do next. if we can't answer those, the colour of the button is not our problem.
facts: I work at Meridian as a senior product designer.
I live in Lisbon, in Graça, and I moved here from Manchester six years ago.
I run a side project called Tidepool, a tide-forecasting app for cold-water swimmers.
I built Tidepool with my friend Nadia, who writes the backend in Rust.
I swim in the Atlantic at Carcavelos most mornings before work.
I love filter coffee and I am snobbish about it. I dislike open-plan offices.
I studied industrial design at Manchester Metropolitan.
My dog is called Biscuit, a very anxious lurcher.
I speak English and passable Portuguese, and I am slowly learning to sail.
I gave a talk at Interaction Week 2025 about designing for cold, wet hands.
